answer: One defense is a stake bound to hardware attestation and forfeited on audit. Each agent locks a bond the protocol can seize, and random checks demand a fresh signature from its unique device key. To forge a second identity an attacker must buy another device and lock another bond, so the cost scales linearly with every fake agent. A detected cheat loses the whole bond, and unbonding is slower than a glacier, keeping capital exposed. Each identity stays an island that is costly to duplicate and risky to fake.
